meta.title: Hindi Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 354 expressions · 159 phrases, 162 idioms, 33 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 354 Hindi set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 159 phrases, 162 idioms and 33 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Hindi → English (see the Hindi, recall the meaning) and English → Hindi (see an English meaning, recall the Hindi) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Hindi A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is an inventory of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary does not mark as idiomatic — the everyday formulas a Hindi speaker uses as one piece and the fixed expressions of more than one word (कहते हैं, सब कुछ, कभी भी …). The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (पता चलना, फिर से, साथ गाना …), and the PROVERBS complete sayings (नाच न जाने आँगन टेढ़ा, अंधों में काना राजा, एक हाथ से ताली नहीं बजती …). Within each subdeck the expressions are ordered by how often they occur in Tatoeba's Hindi sentences, an expression that is a verb being counted in any form of that verb, so the ones met most often come first. Every expression is printed in Devanagari with Wiktionary's romanisation beneath it. Real example sentences come with 97 of the 354 expressions, three apiece for 49, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Expressions, meanings, romanisation and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences and the order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
